guide.pageDescription: The console manages your apps, organizations and account. Walk through these steps to get started in minutes.

step1.description: The console is the entry to all apps. Activated apps live in My Apps; click a card to open the system.
step1.point1: My Apps filters by All / Admin / Client; the Renew action on a card renews a single app.
step1.point2: App Store (owner only): browse and activate new apps individually or per group with Activate All.
step1.point3: Multiple mobile apps with the same name collapse into a folder card.
step1.title: Step 1: Meet the console home

step2.description: Avatar, nickname, password and email/phone binding are maintained in Profile Settings. Complete them on first use.
step2.point1: Upload an avatar (PNG/JPG/JPEG/WebP, up to 2MB) and change your nickname.
step2.point2: Change the password; bind or rebind email and phone (password recovery and notifications depend on them).
step2.point3: View personal messages in the Messages tab; manage API credentials in the Access Tokens tab.
step2.title: Step 2: Complete your profile settings

step3.description: As the organization owner you can maintain organization information, manage memberships, and transfer or delete the organization.
step3.point1: The list shows your organizations and roles (owner/member); click to switch the current organization.
step3.point2: Owner-only actions: edit organization info, transfer and delete the organization.
step3.point3: Members can join other teams via Create / Join Organization; regular members can leave their organization.
step3.point4: Entry: avatar dropdown at top right → Organization Settings, or go directly from this page.
step3.title: Step 3: Organization management (owners)

step4.description: Organization resource quota and app validity are maintained here: users, devices, messages, AI Token and disk space.
step4.point1: The quota card shows usage and limits per resource. Renew or recharge before reaching the limit.
step4.point2: The app quota list shows resource usage per app.
step4.point3: Supports renew (extend validity), recharge (add resources) and redeem codes; also reachable from global search "Renewal Management" or the expiry banner.
step4.title: Step 4: System management (Renewal & Recharge)

step5.description: Need third-party systems or automation scripts to call platform APIs? Create an AccessKey / AccessSecret in Access Tokens, build a JWT, and call open APIs without signing in - the key capability for system integration.
step5.point1: Create a key via New Token: fill in description and expiry, optionally an organization whitelist; the AccessSecret shows only once at creation - save it immediately.
step5.point2: Sign with a JWT library (Go/Python/TypeScript/Java samples provided) using HS256; the payload contains tenantCode, accessKey and expiry exp.
step5.point3: Send headers per request: Authorization: Bearer <JWT>, app-id, tenant-code, Content-Type.
step5.point4: The page includes an online sample Token generator (local signing) and a curl example to verify authentication on the spot; troubleshoot 401 via the page FAQ.
step5.title: Step 5: Open API integration (Access Tokens)

accessToken.point1: Create: Access Tokens tab → New Token; fill in description, choose expiry (never / custom), optionally an organization whitelist (limits accessible organizations).
accessToken.point2: The AccessKey / AccessSecret show only once right after creation - copy and store them immediately; the AccessSecret cannot be viewed again, delete and recreate if leaked.
accessToken.point3: Call: send Authorization: Bearer <JWT>, app-id, tenant-code (organization code) and Content-Type headers per request.
accessToken.point4: The page provides an online sample Token generator (browser-local signing; keys are not uploaded) and Go / Python / TypeScript / Java samples.

sectionCase.point1: The example below calls the get-my-user-info API with a generated JWT to verify the authentication chain:
sectionCase.title: Example: calling an open API

sectionFaq.point1: 401 troubleshooting: JWT expired (exp) → correct accessKey → correct AccessSecret (signature failure) → tenantCode matches headers → token still exists.
sectionFaq.point2: Validity: set exp in the payload (Unix seconds); short validity (e.g. 1 hour) is recommended with re-signing before expiry.
sectionFaq.point3: Organization whitelist: when set, the token can only access whitelisted organizations; if empty, all organizations of the user are accessible.
sectionFaq.title: FAQ

sectionPayload.r1c3: The organization code; must match the tenant-code header. If omitted, the token whitelist and headers decide
sectionPayload.r3c3: Expiry in Unix seconds; without it the token never expires (not recommended in production)
sectionPayload.title: JWT payload fields

sectionSteps.r1c2: Fill in description and expiry in New Token; copy and store the AccessKey and AccessSecret right after creation
sectionSteps.r2c2: Any JWT library: Go golang-jwt/v5, Python PyJWT, TypeScript jose, Java jjwt
sectionSteps.r3c2: Algorithm HS256 with the AccessSecret as key; the payload contains tenantCode and accessKey, plus an exp (e.g. in 1 hour) is recommended
sectionSteps.r4c2: Send headers Authorization: Bearer <JWT>, app-id, tenant-code, Content-Type: application/json
sectionSteps.title: Four steps to integrate

settings.point1: Entry: avatar dropdown at top right → Profile Settings, or visit /user/settings directly.
settings.point2: The top user card supports avatar upload (PNG/JPG/JPEG/WebP, ≤2MB), nickname and password changes.
settings.point3: Settings tab: bind/rebind email and phone, maintain profile (gender).
settings.point4: Messages tab: view and handle personal messages (My Messages in the avatar dropdown points here too).
settings.point5: Access Tokens tab: open API credentials (AccessKey/AccessSecret) for third-party programs to call platform APIs without signing in - see the section below.

sectionSecurity.point1: Change the initial password right after the first sign-in; re-login with the new password afterwards.
sectionSecurity.point2: Email and phone are essential for password recovery and notifications - keep them bound and reachable.
sectionSecurity.point3: Access tokens are equivalent to account credentials. Store them safely; delete and recreate immediately if leaked.
sectionSecurity.title: Account security tips

sectionToken.point1: Purpose: let third-party systems / automation scripts call open APIs without signing in - build a JWT (HS256) with AccessKey + AccessSecret and send Authorization: Bearer <JWT>.
sectionToken.point2: Create: Access Tokens tab → New Token; fill in description and expiry, optionally an organization whitelist (limits accessible organizations).
sectionToken.point3: The AccessSecret shows only once right after creation - copy and store it immediately; if leaked, delete the token and create a new one.
sectionToken.point4: Call: send Authorization / app-id / tenant-code / Content-Type headers; the page provides an online sample Token generator and Go / Python / TypeScript / Java samples.
sectionToken.title: Access Tokens (open API credentials)

faq401.content: Check: 1) is the JWT expired (exp field); 2) is the accessKey correct; 3) is the accessSecret correct (signature verification failed); 4) does the organization code match the request header; 5) has the token been deleted.
faq401.title: Q: Got a 401 error, how to troubleshoot?

faqEmptyCode.content: If the JWT payload omits the organization code, access is decided by the token whitelist and the organization code header. Specifying the organization code in the JWT explicitly is recommended.
faqEmptyCode.title: Q: What happens when the organization code is empty?

faqExp.content: Set the exp field in the JWT payload (Unix seconds). Short validity (e.g. 1 hour = now + 3600s) is recommended. Without exp the JWT never expires (not recommended in production).
faqExp.title: Q: How to set the JWT validity?

faqWhitelist.content: With a whitelist set at token creation, the token can only access whitelisted organizations. The organization code in both the JWT and the header must be in the whitelist. An empty whitelist allows all organizations of the user.
faqWhitelist.title: Q: How does the organization whitelist work?
